statement: For either signed complete inverse operator, a finite periodic weight 0<=h<=1 with L_s h>=q*h and q>=0 gives C_d(a)>=q^d*h(a) at every positive integer a and depth d. For a family of such weights h_i, possibly at different ternary levels, with 0<=q_i<1 and q_i tending to one, the coefficient series at a fixed positive root a is nonsummable if one c>0 satisfies h_i(a)>=c*(1-q_i) for every i. The limiting family and fixed-root lower bound are open premises, not consequences of finite certificates. No Juggler transfer, termination or infinite escape is claimed. Kernel-checked; independent review and advisory statement coverage pending.

For both signed complete inverse coefficient operators, saved positive unit weights at ternary levels 1 through 4, zero on nonunits and normalized by their maximum, satisfy L_s h>=q*h for certified rates 0.285714285, 0.575889816, 0.713279690 and 0.771500620 respectively. Every refined unit residue and every positive exponent are covered by exact integer rows and geometric period folding; independent rational checks construct ordinary odd children. The rates need not be optimal. These eight Python certificates are not kernel-checked data and prove no limiting rate or fixed-root divergence.
